market_summary: US index futures are lower before the open: Dow -0.9%, S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq-100 -0.7% (Yahoo, about 08:00 ET), after Wednesday's pullback from records, with the 10-year at 5.28-5.30% and WTI up 3.75% to about $91.60 on fresh Hormuz shipping attacks and a report that the US military was told to be ready for possible Iran strikes and Brent up about 4% to about $104. Jobless claims were 197,000 (-2,000). Asia was weak as mainland China reopened: Hang Seng -1.4% to 23,785, a three-month low (Hang Seng Tech -2.9%, HSBC and BOC Hong Kong down nearly 5%), Shanghai -0.8% to 3,811, Shenzhen -2.1%; the Nikkei fell 1.4% and the KOSPI 2.6%. On AI hardware, TSMC's September sales were NT$511.86B (+54.6% y/y), putting Q3 about NT$1,494B, above guidance, while Samsung's 107.4T won quarter came in slightly below forecasts and its shares fell. Silicon Data's H100 index was $2.80 on Oct 8 (Oct 7: $2.81), so rental prices are steady at highs. Next: US CPI Wed Oct 14 (AEDT Thu morning), TSMC Q3 Oct 15, Anthropic investor session Oct 14.

AMZN.reason: Down about 0.4% at the open after fewer than 1,000 retail job cuts were confirmed and new Android-based Alexa+ tablets were launched (on sale Oct 14). Nothing changes the thesis before Q3 results around Oct 29.

AXOS.reason: No company news found today and no live quote could be verified; Oct 7 close used. Fiscal Q1 results are due Oct 29, so nothing to act on.

BABA.reason: Up about 1.8% at the open even though Hang Seng Tech fell 2.89% and Alibaba slipped about 1% in Hong Kong on the mainland reopening. Citi raised its target to $193 from $190 ahead of the Nov 24 results; wait for China policy.

ENPH.reason: Down about 1.8% at the open with no new analyst action. Q3 results call is set for Oct 27 at 4:30pm ET, after the Deutsche Bank sell call and target cuts; stay on watch until the print.

FIGR.reason: Down about 1.1% at the open with no news; Goldman and BofA target trims and the strong preliminary Q3 volume are already priced in. Hold.

GOOGL.reason: Up about 0.9% at the open, the one mega-cap in the green. TD Cowen raised its target to $485 from $475, expecting Google Cloud revenue to more than double year on year (82% growth in Q2), and Isomorphic Labs is reportedly in talks to raise at a roughly $40B valuation.

LDI.reason: Down about 2.9% before the open, still a sub-dollar stock with an NYSE compliance notice and no catalyst while mortgage rates and yields stay near highs. Keep trimming into strength.

META.reason: Up about 0.4% at the open, holding up better than other mega-caps while yields and oil rise. No new company catalyst; the Florida and New Mexico cases remain the overhang. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Down about 2.1% at the open, giving back part of the 4.6% gain since Oct 2 as chip stocks slid; the likely reason is profit-taking after a gain of more than 200% this year. Targets raised after investor day stand, so hold and do not chase.

MU.reason: Down about 1.4% before the open and 0.4% after, with memory names weak after Samsung's record Q3 profit (107.4T won) missed the 108.7T forecast. Taiwan workers also voted almost unanimously to authorise a strike (no date); hold.

NFLX.reason: Up about 0.6% at the open despite Morgan Stanley trimming its target to $80 from $83 (Overweight) on flat viewing hours. Q3 results are due Oct 20, so hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: Down 1.0% before the open and 1.2% after it, in line with chips as oil and yields rise and AI debt financing (Broadcom $50B for OpenAI, SpaceX $40B for Nvidia chips) draws attention. Demand signals unchanged; hold.

RKT.reason: Down about 0.6% at the open with no company news. The last verified 30-year mortgage rate average was 7.28% on Oct 1 and the 10-year yield is near 5.3%, so mortgage stocks stay on watch.

TSM.reason: September sales were NT$511.86B (down 0.6% from August, up 54.6% year on year); my arithmetic puts Q3 near US$46.7B at the NT$32 guidance rate, above the top of the US$44.6-45.8B range. The ADR was down about 0.6% at the open on the tech sell-off, so keep adding ahead of the Oct 15 results.

STRIPE.reason: No closed round or tender today; the 2.27x mark is unchanged. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: No closed round or tender. Broadcom is reportedly seeking more than $50B of private debt for OpenAI's custom chips (talks only, nothing signed before year-end), and OpenRouter data showed OpenAI passing Anthropic in weekly model spend. Mark unchanged at 5.43x.

headlines: Futures fall before Thursday's US open: Brent topped $104, the 10-year is near 5.3%, Hang Seng Tech fell 2.9% on China's reopening.
TSMC September sales rose 54.6% to NT$511.86B, putting Q3 above guidance; TSMC reports Oct 15.
Samsung's record Q3 profit came in slightly below forecasts; memory stocks fell, Micron down about 1% premarket.
Broadcom reportedly lining up $50B+ of debt for OpenAI chips; Nvidia and Marvell down 1-2% at the open.
Alphabet: TD Cowen lifts target to $485 on Cloud growth; it was the only mega-cap up at the open.
Next: US CPI Wed Oct 14 (Thu morning AEDT), Anthropic investor session Oct 14, TSMC results Oct 15.
